highlights.title: SpaceX’s ambitious, expensive gamble to replace AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Walter Piecyk, a partner and analyst at LightShed Partners who covers tech, media, and telecom, about SpaceX’s recently announced plan to become a major wireless carrier.
body: Last week, SpaceX agreed to buy a big chunk of low-band spectrum to expand the Starlink network, spectrum that’s been traded around the telecom business for decades now. SpaceX’s ambitious plan is to use that spectrum to help build “the world’s most advanced mobile network.”

Combined with news that the FCC approved the deployment of 15,000 next-gen Starlink satellites and the company’s previous agreement to purchase close to $20 billion worth of EchoStar spectrum last year, it’s now clear SpaceX is serious about competing with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile.

I’ve covered the telecom business for a long time, and I’ve always known that these companies can say they want to do something until they run into the harsh reality of how expensive it is to actually do it. The telecom graveyard of pivots, bad ideas, and failed acquisitions is vast.

highlights.title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
highlights.summary: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there.
body: Before being fired five days into her stint as White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia spent much of the day attempting to explain her past.

Throughout her brief tenure, Zacharia’s résumé was the source of much intrigue. Foremost was the fact that despite claiming to be an attorney for much of her career, she never actually passed the California bar, as she was eventually forced to admit. Another element of her professional history, WIRED reported, was a role as an affiliate marketer for Beachbody, a fitness multilevel marketing company.

WIRED has now uncovered new details of her relationship to an AI-powered rare-earth mining operation called NRED Intelligent Mining, which counts former Department of Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem as a strategic adviser.

On June 24, NRED—then known as NovaRed Mining, a small copper-and-gold exploration company in Vancouver, Canada—issued a press release to share that Zacharia, who had left a role as a DHS spokesperson two months before, was joining the advisory board alongside Noem.

highlights.title: 2026 Has Been a Surprisingly Excellent Year for Shooters
highlights.summary: All the way back in January, it seemed like 2026 might be a rough year for fans of shooters. Highguard ’s launch and almost immediate delaunch created an anxiety around the genre that was hard to shake.
body: Rumors of the shooter’s demise were greatly exaggerated, it turns out. Looking back at the year from October’s vantage point, 2026 has turned out to be a landmark year for the genre. While sales have been erratic at times, this year has given us plenty of big-budget and indie shooters alike that have revitalized a category that needed some fresh blood.

Xbox has been a major player in that charge, despite having a disastrous year from a business perspective. Even so, the studios working under the publisher have still found a way to deliver a handful of hits. Chief among them is Gear of War: E-Day, which has been a hit with critics and players alike since launch. It’s a highly polished throwback to the golden age of cover-based shooters, one that packs a lot of delicious brutality into a lore-expanding prequel campaign. With Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 positioned as a similar return to glory, Xbox could wind up with two behemoths on its hands this year.

highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: Mahershala Ali Cries Recalling ‘Moonlight’ Scene, Keeps Quiet on ‘Spider-Verse’ at London Talk: ‘I’ve Got to Be Careful’
highlights.summary: Mahershala Ali broke down in tears on stage at the BFI London Film Festival on Saturday as he recalled the young boy at the heart of “Moonlight.” The Barry Jenkins drama won him one of his two Oscars and recently marked its 10th anniversary.
body: “Any time people put flesh on the bones of those who haven’t been seen or had their moment, I think it’s important,” he said once he had composed himself. “I think ‘Moonlight’ was able to make those characters people… make it personal.”

To play Juan, Ali drew on a man he had known all his life, an uncle-like figure he had grown up playing basketball with who also worked as a substitute teacher. The man was arrested and sent to prison while Ali was in college, which left the actor stunned.
“I thought of him a lot in the making of the film because of how human everyone was in my environment and in my upbringing,” Ali said.

He was candid about the backlash that followed “Green Book,” in which he played pianist Don Shirley opposite Viggo Mortensen. It was his first role of that magnitude, and the backlash included the controversy over what Shirley’s family had and hadn’t sanctioned.

highlights.title: ‘It feels like the light is pushing the darkness apart’: Gellért Gombai’s best phone picture
highlights.summary: The photographer was holidaying with his family when two shadows became a plaything for his young son. Gellért Gombai, his wife and two children spend much of the year at their home in Budapest, Hungary, but most of their summers in Alsóörs.
body: On this particular day, the family had eaten hotdogs for lunch, before Gombai had taken the kids, Lóci and Janka, to the playground. “Lóci, who was five at the time, was jumping between two shadows – one from a changing room, and the other from a building’s roof,” he says. “I asked him to stay still for a few minutes while I got the shot, and he lay like this on the ground. He’s a big-hearted little clown; I’m so glad he’s my son.” When he showed the children, “Janka immediately asked me to take the same shot of her, which often happens. Lóci said it looked like he was among mountains, or as though a monster was about to eat him.”

Gombai applied his phone’s “dramatic cool” filter, and made some minor adjustments. “I really liked the slightly metaphysical spaces created by light and shadow,” he says. “If I forget for a moment it’s my son, I see a carefree form lying in the light while the darkness has bitten a large piece out of the space. Even still, it doesn’t feel sad to me. I have the feeling that the light is pushing the darkness apart.”

highlights.title: How Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base
highlights.summary: With ia.i, a conversational interface, and the IARA governance platform, Itaú is applying its AI First strategy to customers and employees — in one of Brazil’s most regulated sectors.
body: Creating a close, personalized experience for millions of customers in a country like Brazil is, first and foremost, a question of simplicity rather than of models.
“Much of it is about making something simple, direct, and useful, delivering a direct benefit to the customer, and making the technology almost unnoticeable,” says Carlos Eduardo Mazzei, CTO of Itaú.

The standard he describes is demanding: the solution must solve a real everyday problem and be direct, simple, and memorable. Technology serves as the means, never as the centerpiece of the experience.

There is demand for this. A study by Itaú in partnership with Grupo Consumoteca shows that 80% of Brazilians want to better organize their financial lives and seek more effective support for decisions, and that 65% would like technologies that act as a financial copilot, providing ongoing guidance.

highlights.title: Whalefall Isn't Really About a Whale, Says Josh Brolin
highlights.summary: While at New York Comic Con 2026, a week before the film’s release, Polygon caught up with stars Josh Brolin and Austin Abrams, as well as Kraus and Duffield, to talk about the biggest challenges of bringing this book to the big screen, as well as what the movie is really about.
body: Whalefall is now in theaters. Based on the novel by Daniel Kraus ( Angel Down ), who also co-wrote the screenplay with director Brian Duffield ( No One Will Save You, Cocaine Bear ), Whalefall is about a scuba diver (Austin Abrams) looking for the remains of his father ( Josh Brolin ) in the Pacific Ocean. However, while he’s on his expedition, he gets swallowed by an enormous sperm whale. With only an hour’s worth of oxygen, he must free himself from inside the whale.

According to Kraus, the toughest part of the inside-the-whale experience was bringing to life the stomach of the whale — or, more accurately, the first stomach, as sperm whale stomachs consist of four separate chambers.
Austin Abrams, who stars in Whalefall as diver Jay Gardiner, pointed to the same scene as the most difficult, saying the hardest part of the film was “the compression, being squeezed.”
As much as the movie is about a guy getting swallowed by a whale, neither Kraus nor Duffield ever saw the whale as the film’s villain.

highlights.title: Mahershala Ali Put His Two Oscars Into a Cabinet: “I Felt a Sense of Accomplishment, Not Fulfillment”
highlights.summary: In London, the star also discussed playing people who "haven’t been seen," nearly going crazy on 'True Detective,' police brutality and how 'Green Book' made him feel like a "golden boy," followed by vitriol.
body: BAFTA and two-time Oscar winner Mahershala Ali shared insights into his work, career and new existential crime thriller, Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, at a crowded London cinema on Saturday.
He spoke during a Screen Talk session as part of the 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival (LFF), which wraps up on Sunday.

How did he feel about the two Oscar wins? “I felt a sense of accomplishment, which is not fulfillment,” the star shared. “Those are different experiences. … Even gratitude is different from accomplishment, which is different from fulfillment. I feel I’m closer to that space now of feeling fulfilled on some level in terms of the work.”

In that context, he pointed out that his newest role is only his second lead role after Swan Song. Indeed, in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, Ali stars as Latif, a devout Muslim and contract killer who travels across Houston in an effort to protect his three children following the death of his wife. He faces dangerous obstacles, including John Cho’s Haun Yoon, an Army veteran and militant church leader who is determined to destroy what he deems great evils.

highlights.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
highlights.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.
body: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

highlights.title: The Best Transformers Movie That No One Watched Finds New Life on Streaming
highlights.summary: Under director Michael Bay, Paramount built a billion-dollar franchise across five live-action Transformers movies. But after Bay's final turn behind the camera, 2017's Transformers: The Last Knight, the robots-in-disguise franchise started to go in unpredictable new directions.
body: Paramount swerved in 2024 with one of the best Transformers movies to date, the animated prequel Transformers One. While it didn't light up the box office or please every Transformers fan, the origin story of Optimus Prime and Megatron is finding a new life on streaming.

Transformers One was recently added to Netflix after a multiyear run on Paramount Plus. Netflix audiences are giving the animated feature another shot, according to streaming data from FlixPatrol. Transformers One quickly landed in the top 10 most-watched movies on Netflix this week, charting at No. 6 in the U.S. It's nestled between Twilight — it's officially "Hoa hoa hoa" season — and the animated comedy Ice Age.

Netflix viewers are right to give Transformers One the overdue attention it deserves. As we said in our review of the film, it's "sweet, occasionally heartbreaking, and utterly convincing in telling an origin story for friends-turned-foes Optimus Prime and Megatron. Thanks to its strong cast and a solid story buttressed by a classic hero’s journey, Transformers One has a spark that we’ve rarely seen in a Transformers flick..."

highlights.title: ‘The Angry Birds Movie 3’ Unpacked by VFX Supervisor, Including Red’s Redesign and Character-Effects Automation: ’He’s Similar by Choice’
highlights.summary: The red-feathered hero of “The Angry Birds Movie 3” looks reassuringly familiar, but DNEG Animation had to rebuild much of him to bring the franchise back to theaters.
body: The technical handover was anything but straightforward. In fact, proprietary grooming, rigging and surfacing tools used on the predecessors could not simply be transferred to DNEG’s pipeline. “We had to start from this. A plucked chicken version of Red,” Harboun joked, displaying a bare digital model. Even its underlying geometry needed reworking before the team could reconstruct its feathers.

The result deliberately avoided a radical makeover. Red’s plumage became slightly softer, while his eyes and beak gained firmer, more toy-like surfaces. “Once an IP becomes popular, it kind of belongs to the fans, and we have to respect that,” Harboun said. “We can’t just add our own spin just to give our mark.”

The studio scrutinized the earlier movies frame by frame. “We analyzed the past movies to find the unwritten rules of animation,” he explained. Animators cataloged the angles of Red’s beak, the geometry of his narrowed eyes and the boundaries beyond which a stretched expression stopped feeling like Red. The lessons became a style guide and a reusable library of facial expressions.

Part of the resurgence can be tied to the fact that they’re cool now with younger generations — following the revival of tape decks and vinyl. highlights.title: Fostering community amid Kendall Square’s innovation
highlights.summary: The 18th annual Kendall Square Association Annual Meeting explored how new technologies could be a force for shared prosperity in society.
body: Kendall Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is often cited as the most innovative square mile in the world. But when the Kendall Square Association gathered local stakeholders for its 18th Annual Meeting Thursday, the conversation focused on innovation primarily in the context of community.

The event, which took place at the nonprofit startup incubator The Engine, attracted people from across Cambridge, including business leaders, elected officials, local residents, and students, for a night of local food and conversation about the advance of technologies like artificial intelligence and what they mean for society.

“How can we make AI not an enemy of work, but a tool for workers to expand their capabilities and build new expertise or do new things?” asked MIT Institute Professor Daron Acemoglu in a keynote talk. “The world is at a point in time where we need new innovations and new adaptations to growing challenges.”

Acemoglu’s keynote was one of several presentations at the event, which also featured music from the Kendall Square Orchestra, a vote on new KSA board members, and awards for organizations making a positive impact through innovation.

highlights.title: Early Modern Warfare 4 Consensus Unanimous That It Features On Of The Best COD Campaigns Ever
highlights.summary: The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign released on Oct. 16 for those who pre-ordered the game digitally, so first reactions to it are finally rolling in. So far, sentiment around this part of the new Call of Duty is positive, with many fans praising the campaign.
body: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's campaign takes the action to South Korea, as Price fights against Makarov and a new threat called The Archer reaches new heights just as a war between North and South Korea breaks out. It's a high-stakes political and military thriller, and has some open-ended levels that tease out the impending DMZ mode. While Black Ops 7's campaign was one of the most derided aspects of last year's Call of Duty, the opposite is the case for Modern Warfare 4.

A quick look at the top posts on the Modern Warfare 4 subreddit shows how much players are loving the campaign. User Havkas called it the "best campaign since original trilogy," elaborating that it "plays like a perfect blend of the modern entries and the original trilogy." This sentiment is felt across the subreddit, as fans see the campaign as a return to form for the Modern Warfare franchise after some relatively weaker recent campaigns. In one comment, user Resting-Tiger goes as far as to say the game has " MW2 OG levels of storytelling," favorably comparing it to one of the best Call of Duty campaigns ever.

highlights.title: Apple’s HomeView is just the latest threat to online recipe writers
highlights.summary: When Apple revealed the HomeView to the world, it did so with an unusual ad for the company: Instead of pristine, polished tech in immaculate rooms, it's a three-minute look at the messy, frantic morning routine of a family of five.
body: Its simplified, hands-free instructions strip out much of what’s essential to online recipes.

The HomeView is just the latest in a long line of websites, browser extensions, and smart home gadgets with the same promise: that it can take an online recipe and strip it down to the essentials. Instead of scrolling a lengthy webpage that might range from helpful cooking instructions to seemingly irrelevant personal anecdotes, with the recipe itself way down at the bottom, you simply get ingredient lists, cooking instructions, and timers, all navigable hands-free with voice controls and Siri AI. No distractions, no unnecessary text, and no need to deal with a touchscreen while you’re wrist-deep in a chicken carcass. The appeal is obvious.

highlights.title: Steam's Achievement Sets beta aims to stop new content breaking your completion status
highlights.summary: Valve is beta testing Steam Achievement Sets, a feature that lets developers group a game's achievements into collections.
body: In an announcement, the company said that games "live longer than ever, continuing to receive updates through new DLC, expansions, and seasons", but that achievements added with new content "can be hard to discover and can accidentally break the completion status of players who have already finished the game".

That's why developers can now specify the number of sets and the purpose of each "to match their game's specific needs", so one game might group its achievements into single-player and multiplayer groups, while another could use eight class-based sets. Players still unlock achievements as usual, and Steam then sorts what they've unlocked into the developer-created sets, which Valve says makes it "easier to see what you have completed and to find other related achievements you can unlock next".
Each set has its own progress bar, and completing one adds a "set complete" trophy to the player's profile. If new achievements are later added to a set, completion is "preserved".
points: Valve is beta testing Steam Achievement Sets, a feature that lets developers group a game's achievements into collections.

highlights.title: Homemade McGriddles
highlights.summary: The key part of any good copycat recipe is that one hard-to-pinpoint flavor component that makes the whole thing light up the nostalgia part of your brain. Without it, even a delicious meal feels a little bit like a letdown.
body: Make homemade breakfast sandwiches better than the fast-food classic using instant pancake (or biscuit) mix with fluffy maple-glazed pancakes, eggs, American cheese, and crispy bacon.

Because we’re going to the trouble of making this at home, there have to be a few upgrades. Greek yogurt in the batter adds a boost of tang and protein and keeps the pancakes firm enough while cooking to keep their shape. A fluffy folded egg bakes alongside thick-cut bacon in the oven. But, perhaps most importantly, use the nicest maple syrup you can find. It’s a good thing they reheat well, so I can enjoy my nostalgic little breakfast treat throughout the week.

Arrange two racks to divide the oven into thirds. Heat the oven to 350ºF. Meanwhile, arrange 6 halved thick-cut bacon slices in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet. Place on the lower rack while the oven is heating up and bake until crisp, 25 to 40 minutes total. Meanwhile, make the pancakes and eggs.

highlights.title: Encryption Is Getting Squeezed From All Sides
highlights.summary: Canada’s planned surveillance law is the latest grim step in a series of threats to encryption that are spreading around the world.
body: Oh, Canada. The Great White North is the latest country to contemplate legislation that could essentially mandate backdoors and increase data retention in encrypted services. The proposed changes have prompted the Canadian anti-censorship company Psiphon VPN—which keeps millions of Iranians online during repressive internet shutdowns —to say it will leave the country if the bill passes. And Psiphon is not the only one.

Encrypted messaging app Signal has said it would exit the Canadian market because the legislation would require unacceptable changes to its open source projects. Apple and Meta have criticized the bill, and DuckDuckGo and NordVPN say they would consider pulling their services, too. But as countries around the world contemplate similar legislation, even larger questions begin to emerge about which states or regions could differentiate themselves as being safe havens for privacy services if global hostility to encryption continues to rise.

highlights.title: Championship roundup: Zemura seals Watford reprieve for Dionisi
highlights.summary: Watford out of bottom three after beating Charlton 2-0. Middlesbrough 2-2 Cardiff; Millwall 2-2 Lincoln. Watford lifted the pressure on Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters’ rebellion against the owner, Gino Pozzo, with a deserved 2-0 win against a sluggish Charlton side.
body: After shipping nine goals in calamitous defeats by Burnley and Cardiff, Dionisi’s side had slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo. But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and the substitute Jordan Zemura – the Zimbabwe defender’s first for the club – extended Charlton’s worrying run to eight games without a win as the Addicks were booed off at Vicarage Road.

Despite the mood of insurrection swirling around Pozzo on social media, protests against his 14-year ownership outside the ground before kick-off were limited and Watford kept their first clean sheet in 210 days with only their second win in three months.

Jake Cooper’s scrambled equaliser rescued a point for Millwall as they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Lincoln. The Imps looked on course to put Wednesday’s 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubiș and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at the Den. There was some controversy around the second goal, though, as what looked a clear handball by Reeco Hackett in the buildup was missed by the assistant stood close by.

The sports-tourism market was estimated to be worth $1.16 trillion in 2025 and now makes up about 10 percent of the tourism economy itself. Travelers want to do more than just catch a game; they want to get on the court with Grand Slam winners and cheer in the VIP grandstands at Formula 1 races—and increasingly, it's top hotels that are helping facilitate that kind of VIP access.
